subject: psychology
title: Psychological Approaches: Behaviourism & SLT
welcome_lead: From Pavlov to Bandura — learning theories in detail.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology behaviourism Pavlov Skinner Bandura social learning theory.
final_note: Behaviourism keeps it observable; SLT brings the mind back.

concepts.def: Conditioned response — learned reflex to CS.
Reinforcement after unpredictable number of responses — gambling.
Learning from observed consequences for others.
Adopting model's behaviours — SLT mediating factor.

walkthroughs.body_html: Pavlov (1902): bell + meat powder repeated → bell alone produces salivation. Key principles: acquisition, extinction (CS without UCS), spontaneous recovery, generalisation (similar stimuli), discrimination. Watson & Rayner (1920) conditioned Little Albert to fear a white rat.

Skinner (1953): behaviour shaped by consequences. Variable ratio schedules are most resistant to extinction — explaining gambling. Skinner box showed rats press levers for food and avoid shocks. Punishment is less effective than reinforcement.

Bandura, Ross & Ross (1961): children imitated adult Bobo doll aggression. 1963 version showed vicarious reinforcement matters — children who saw the model rewarded imitated most. Four mediational processes: attention, retention, reproduction, motivation.

mcqs.q: Which reinforcement schedule is most resistant to extinction?
